taylor_quinney.method: Set 90 percent plastic-work heat conversion, to be sensitivity-tested
assumptions: Not a Ck45 batch measurement or part of Jaspers fitted card; Jaspers p. 93 assumed all deformation energy becomes heat
limitations: No identified parameter covariance or uncertainty; no MPM calibration
Exploratory candidate: successful execution does not establish experimental validation
Different normalized AISI1045 lot: not the measured 2024 Ck45 tensile fit
Primary thesis documents dynamic strain-aging and pronounced JC discrepancies around 500 degC
Tm=1733 K from original Table5.3; do not substitute Klippel2024 typical1773 K or Burns2013 value1490 degC
Elastic and thermophysical constants use Klippel2024 typical literature values; beta=.9 is an explicit additional assumption
Migrated numeric constants unchanged; active finite law is described by constitutive_convention
Experimental plastic strain/rate applicability intervals have not been established here
Tref and Tm delimit the implemented thermal normalization, not an experimental validity interval
Friction is a pair/contact assumption in the case thermal section, not a material constant

constitutive_convention.kinematics: 3D finite Hencky J2 under Fzz=1 plane strain; Fp remains 3D
constitutive_convention.stress: JC resistance is Cauchy; local return uses q_tau=J*Y
constitutive_convention.beta: fraction of plastic work converted to heat; beta=0 retains thermal softening
constitutive_convention.solid_range: Stop before T>=Tm; no phase change or physical melt model
constitutive_convention.properties: constant density reference, E, nu, cp, k and beta; no thermal expansion

metadata.purpose: Development at 25 m/min; full cutting target, not experimental replication
assumptions: Horizontal +x, rigid tool, stationary stock, plane strain with full 3D constitutive history
1.5 x 0.6 mm stock, 1 mm width, 100 um uncut thickness, 25 um edge, 10/7 degree angles are explicit design choices
Initial physical gap is zero; constant speed starts at t=0, no undocumented ramp
Fix x/y on one bottom grid-coefficient band; actual material support still requires verification
Coulomb mu=0.35, friction heat partition 0.9 to piece, tool temperature from material initial value: assumptions requiring sensitivity
Insulated material exterior; zero tool conductance; no convective or radiative loss in this diagnostic model
Projected thermal reference with eta=1; stabilization and dense limits require accuracy/cost evaluation
Finite JC properties/ranges from versioned card; constants, no damage, thermal expansion, wear or self-contact
No stationary window, no accepted h/dt or experimental comparison yet
Target 0.5 mm advance is provisional; preflight guards may prevent execution at this resolution
